title: Negation, scope and presupposition
orientation: This permanent extension develops topics beyond the daily introductory treatment. Read its definition and foundational explanation first, then work through the examples and progressively deeper analysis. The linked exercises require reasons as well as labels. The entry remains available independently of course completion.
outcomes: Distinguish the relevant grammatical and interpretive concepts.
Apply qualified structural analysis to unfamiliar examples.
Identify contextual or theoretical limits rather than overgeneralising.
Produce and revise an original example with a reasoned explanation.

modules.title: Negation, polarity and quantifier scope
modules.definition: Negation rejects a proposition or a relevant part of its meaning. Scope is the portion of a structure or interpretation affected by an operator such as not, every or only. Surface word order is evidence for scope, but context and prosody can also matter.
foundation: English commonly forms a negative finite clause with not after an auxiliary: The clerk has not replied. Where an ordinary lexical verb has no auxiliary, do-support is normally used: The clerk did not reply. Be can itself carry negation: The office is not open. A negative subject can make the clause negative without an additional negative verb: Nobody replied. Do not add didn’t simply because the intended message is negative. The difference between no and not is structural as well as semantic: no can determine a noun phrase, as in no reply, whereas not commonly negates a clause or phrase. These examples describe ordinary standard constructions, not every historically or regionally established pattern.
intermediate: Scope changes meaning. Not all applications were successful means that at least one was unsuccessful; it does not by itself assert that any succeeded. No applications were successful states zero success. In an everyday conversation, a speaker saying not all may encourage an inference that some did succeed, but that extra inference should not be built into an exact answer key without context. All the applications were not successful can be unclear between intended readings for some audiences; revise explicitly when the distinction matters. Quantified noun phrases can also interact: Every reviewer read a report can allow a different report for each reviewer or one report shared by all. A careful paraphrase states the intended relationship.
advanced: Any, ever and related expressions occur naturally in many negative, interrogative and conditional environments: I did not find any errors; Did you find any?; If you find any, call me. They are not exclusively negative words. Free-choice any in Any qualified applicant may apply has a different distribution and interpretation. Negative concord, as in dialectal I didn’t see nobody with one intended negation, is a systematic feature of some varieties; it is not ordinarily the edited standard British or American pattern taught as the course default. For that default, use I didn’t see anybody or I saw nobody. Distinguish this concord from two independently meaningful negatives, such as It is not impossible.
expert: Logical paraphrase is useful but not a replacement for actual usage. Not impossible leaves possibility open; it does not guarantee likelihood or success. Negative questions often convey expectations, and an answer should clarify the proposition: Yes, she called or No, she did not call. Focus and contrast can narrow negation: I did not criticise the design because it was expensive may deny the criticism or deny that expense was the reason, depending on context. An assessment must stipulate the intended reading or ask learners to explain the ambiguity. Formal writing benefits from explicit scope when costs, obligations or permissions depend on it; unfamiliarity alone does not make a negative construction ungrammatical.

patterns.meaning: Denies universal inclusion; it does not entail a positive number within the group.

patterns.form: no + noun phrase / auxiliary + not + remaining verb phrase
patterns.meaning: Negative noun-phrase determination and clause negation have different structures.

examples.sentence: Not all the windows were locked.
examples.analysis: At least one window was not locked; the sentence alone does not say how many were locked.
This states zero locked windows in the relevant set.

examples.sentence: Each inspector received a different folder.
examples.analysis: Different makes an intended distribution explicit, rather than leaving it to the scope of an indefinite folder.

contrasts.note: The first rejects impossibility. It does not entail the probability judgement in the second.

exceptions: Any also has free-choice uses outside negative environments, so never define it as a word used only in negatives or questions.
Multiple negative forms may express dialectal negative concord, litotes or genuinely separate negations. Identify the construction and editorial target before revising.

mistakes.problem: Not all passed means that some definitely passed.
mistakes.repair: Not all passed entails that universal passing did not occur; it can be true if nobody passed.
mistakes.reason: A common conversational suggestion is not the same as an entailment.

mistakes.problem: I didn’t see nobody is meaningless in every variety.
mistakes.repair: For edited standard English, use I didn’t see anybody; some dialects systematically use negative concord.
mistakes.reason: Register/variety is the issue, not absence of linguistic structure.

glossary.definition: The part of an interpretation affected by an operator.
glossary.example: Not all rejected differs from all rejected.

glossary.definition: Multiple negative forms associated with a single semantic negation in a variety.
glossary.example: Some dialects use I didn’t see nobody for I saw nobody.

glossary.definition: An expression whose distribution or interpretation is sensitive to environments such as negation or questions.
glossary.example: Any in I did not see any is licensed in a negative context.

modules.title: Presupposition, entailment and contextual interpretation
modules.definition: A presupposition is information an utterance normally treats as already taken for granted, often associated with a particular expression. An entailment follows from what is asserted under the relevant reading. Pragmatic inferences also depend on context, expectations and the purpose of the utterance.
foundation: Compare Leena opened the gate with Leena has stopped opening the gate at dawn. The first asserts an opening event. The second normally takes a previous practice for granted while asserting its cessation. A reader who never knew of that practice may accommodate it: provisionally add it to the shared information. Accommodation is an interpretation process, not independent evidence that the practice existed. In factual academic or professional writing, do not smuggle an unverified premise into a sentence merely by presenting it as familiar. Ask what the source explicitly states, what it presupposes and what the writer is only inferring. The grammatical form can influence these distinctions without guaranteeing real-world truth.
intermediate: Expressions often discussed as presupposition triggers include stop, again, definite descriptions and factive predicates such as regret. The coordinator regrets that the hearing was postponed normally treats the postponement as a fact while reporting an attitude toward it. Negating the attitude usually leaves that background assumption: The coordinator does not regret that the hearing was postponed. This persistence under negation is a useful diagnostic, not an exceptionless definition. Questions and conditionals provide further tests, and interpretations can depend on local context. Again commonly signals recurrence, but its exact attachment and focus can matter. Do not turn a short list of triggers into a mechanical method that ignores the whole sentence.
advanced: Entailment and conversational inference require different reasoning. Some applicants arrived late is compatible with all applicants arriving late under its basic existential reading, although ordinary conversation often suggests not all. By contrast, The applicants all arrived late entails arrival for each member of the relevant group under that reading. A stronger statement cannot automatically be substituted for a weaker source statement in a précis. Likewise, The service was not unhelpful can convey restrained praise without being equivalent in tone or commitment to The service was excellent. Grammar provides possible structures; register and conversational expectations help explain why a writer chooses one rather than another. Preserve both propositional qualifications and the force of cautious claims when paraphrasing.
expert: Presupposition research contains substantive theoretical disagreements about conventional meaning, speaker assumptions, projection and cancellation. This course introduces practical diagnostics rather than claiming one short account resolves those debates. Presuppositions sometimes fail to project through a larger structure, and a continuation can reject or suspend an apparent background assumption. It is therefore safer to say normally presupposes under this reading than always proves. In editing, a loaded question such as Who approved the alteration? may invite the assumption that somebody did, while Nobody approved it rejects that assumption. The response is not grammatically defective merely because it declines the proposed premise. Expert analysis specifies the reading, context and evidence, and distinguishes grammatical acceptability from the truth or fairness of the assumption.

patterns.meaning: Normally presents P as a background fact while asserting X’s regret.
Normally backgrounds earlier Y-activity while asserting that the activity has ceased.

examples.sentence: The caretaker has stopped opening the side gate.
examples.analysis: Earlier opening is normally backgrounded; cessation is asserted.

examples.sentence: The caretaker has not stopped opening the side gate.
examples.analysis: The negative commonly preserves the assumption of earlier opening while rejecting cessation.

examples.sentence: If there ever was a side gate, the caretaker no longer uses it.
examples.analysis: The explicit conditional context can suspend existence assumptions that a simpler definite description might encourage.

contrasts.note: The first does not entail the second. An expectation that some excludes all is not a universal truth-conditional rule.

exceptions: Projection and cancellation vary by trigger, embedding and context; a single negation test is not a complete proof.
Backgrounding a claim does not verify it. Source-based writing must check the factual premise as well as the grammar.

mistakes.problem: The source says visits rose during the trial; therefore the trial caused the increase.
mistakes.repair: Visits rose during the trial; the source does not by itself establish the cause.
mistakes.reason: A temporal relation does not entail a causal relation.

mistakes.problem: Closed always entails that it had previously been open.
mistakes.repair: A stative description such as The office is closed need not entail prior openness; an eventive reading needs its own context.
mistakes.reason: Do not add the presupposition no longer without evidence for a change of state.

glossary.definition: Information an utterance normally treats as taken for granted under a reading.
glossary.example: Stopped visiting commonly backgrounds earlier visits.

glossary.definition: A consequence that must hold if the asserted proposition is true under the relevant reading.
glossary.example: All members voted entails that each member in the relevant group voted.

glossary.definition: Adjusting contextual assumptions to interpret information presented as already shared.
glossary.example: A reader may infer a previously unmentioned gate from the side gate.

questions.prompt: Which follows necessarily from Not all the tickets were sold?
options: At least one ticket was not sold.
At least one ticket was sold.
questions.why: Denying universal sale entails at least one unsold ticket. It does not by itself establish any sales or a precise proportion.

questions.prompt: Compare Not all the windows were locked with No windows were locked.
questions.model: The first denies that every window was locked; the second states that none were locked. The first alone does not guarantee that any were locked.
rubric: Do not convert a possible conversational suggestion into a necessary conclusion.
alternatives: Accept another analysis that identifies the same grammatical relationships and preserves the stated meaning; explain any terminology difference.

questions.prompt: Give two explicit readings of Every reviewer read a report.
questions.model: For every reviewer, there was some report that reviewer read; it need not be the same for all. Alternatively, there was one particular report every reviewer read. The first reading does not require pairwise different reports.
rubric: State the distribution of reports explicitly.
Do not assume the indefinite must refer to one shared report.
alternatives: Accept another analysis that identifies the same grammatical relationships and preserves the stated meaning; explain any terminology difference.

questions.prompt: For ordinary edited British English, revise I didn’t see nobody while explaining why the original is not meaningless in every dialect.
questions.model: I didn’t see anybody. The original can exemplify systematic negative concord in some varieties, although it is not the editorial default here.
rubric: Identify regional structure without stigmatising speakers.
alternatives: Accept another analysis that identifies the same grammatical relationships and preserves the stated meaning; explain any terminology difference.

questions.prompt: What does The curator regrets that the painting was moved normally background?
options: That the painting was never moved
That the curator is unable to speak
That the curator moved it personally
questions.why: The factive regret construction normally takes the painting’s move as given. It does not identify the mover.

questions.prompt: Use a negative version to explore what The caretaker has stopped opening the gate normally presupposes.
questions.model: The caretaker has not stopped opening the gate commonly still backgrounds earlier opening, while rejecting cessation. This is a diagnostic under the normal reading, not an exceptionless theorem.
rubric: Identify earlier activity and the changed asserted content.
Qualify the diagnostic for context and embedding.
alternatives: Accept another analysis that identifies the same grammatical relationships and preserves the stated meaning; explain any terminology difference.

questions.prompt: Source: Applications rose during the publicity campaign. Repair The campaign caused applications to rise without inventing evidence.
questions.model: Applications rose during the publicity campaign; the source does not establish that the campaign caused the rise.
rubric: Retain the observed rise and its time relation.
Remove rather than invent support for the causal inference.
alternatives: Accept another analysis that identifies the same grammatical relationships and preserves the stated meaning; explain any terminology difference.

questions.prompt: Explain why not unhelpful need not be interchangeable with excellent in a review.
questions.model: Not unhelpful rejects an unfavourable judgement and may offer restrained praise. Excellent expresses a much stronger positive evaluation.
rubric: Distinguish logical compatibility, degree and rhetorical force.
Preserve the speaker’s commitment when paraphrasing.
alternatives: Accept another analysis that identifies the same grammatical relationships and preserves the stated meaning; explain any terminology difference.

writing.prompt: Write a short explanatory note comparing not all with none and illustrating a qualified presupposition diagnostic.
writing.model: Not all the doors were locked means that at least one door was unlocked; it does not prove that any were locked. No doors were locked is the explicit zero-locking claim. The caretaker has stopped opening the side gate normally takes earlier opening for granted, and that background assumption commonly survives in has not stopped. This negative comparison is useful evidence for a presupposition, but context and embedding can affect interpretation. Neither grammatical form verifies that the gate really existed or that the reported practice occurred.
rubric: Explain the difference between denying universality and asserting zero.
Use stop and its negative to illustrate a normal background assumption.
Qualify the diagnostic rather than treating projection as exceptionless or as factual verification.
alternatives: Accept another analysis that identifies the same grammatical relationships and preserves the stated meaning; explain any terminology difference.

checklist: I can explain the distinctions in my own words.
I can test a proposed analysis against context and examples.
